name: Soft Green
lede: Soft Green is a muted, yellow-leaning green, modifier grammar for 'soft' plus Green, and the phrase was already common in English print decades before the 2010 crowd survey that formally named this shade.

sections.title: A modifier, and an older phrase
sections.body:
Our graph files this as a modifier compound, 'soft' added to the family word [[green]], surveyed by xkcd in 2010 rather than drawn from any book, pigment or place [1]. The phrase itself peaks earlier in English print, around the 1870s, and rose fastest in the 1820s, by Google Books' count across every sense of the words, which can include a landscape or a season as easily as a fashion color [2]. No ISCC-NBS or Ridgway filing exists in our library for this exact modifier name, so its naming beyond the 2010 survey is undocumented [1].

Its real nearest look-alike is [[mantis]], more vivid than this muted green, with [[emerald]] close behind, also more vivid, and [[arcadian-green]] a little further out, duller than both [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this green in 3 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, with the within-painting lens counting 2 — rarer than 82 percent of the named colors we track [4]. The two matches span from 1795 to 1914, too thin a sample for any century trend, and neither painting has an attributed artist on file, so no painter claim follows either [4].
